lessons.title: Never assume /tmp is writable on Termux
lessons.symptom: Piped jq extractions to /tmp/*.json silently fail with Permission denied.
lessons.root_cause: Termux does not guarantee /tmp is writable. $TMPDIR is the correct path.
lessons.fix: Always write to $TMPDIR (guaranteed writable) or .cache/ within the project.

lessons.title: Never assume JSON field names — inspect with jq keys first
lessons.symptom: ADR catalog produced 0 records despite 36 allocation records existing.
lessons.root_cause: Query used .allocations (null) but actual field is .allocated (array of 36).
lessons.fix: Run jq "keys" before consuming external JSON.

lessons.title: Heredoc on stdin overrides pipe, breaking Python read()
lessons.symptom: Python extractor produced empty output despite git show returning data.
lessons.root_cause: out=$(git show ... | python3 - <<'PY') consumed heredoc as stdin, not git show output. sys.stdin.read() returned the heredoc text, not the ADR markdown.
lessons.fix: Write Python to a real file. Pipe git show into that file via python3 script.py. Never mix heredoc-in-subshell with piped input.
lessons.evidence: 12/12 SKIP invalid record — all with empty $out from Python.

lessons.title: Gate existence is not gate coverage
lessons.symptom: Empty adr-catalog.json passed all gates and shipped in commit.
lessons.root_cause: No gate asserted non-empty catalog content. G01–G04 checked file presence and schema, not results.
lessons.fix: Every artifact whose content matters must have a gate asserting non-trivial content (length > 0, expected anomalies present/absent).

lessons.title: jq -s on NDJSON produces one element per line, not a nested array
lessons.symptom: Cannot index string with string (adr_id) when merging allocation registry with canonical ADR NDJSON.
lessons.root_cause: jq -s slurps each JSON value as a top-level element. NDJSON has one value per line, so jq -s produces N elements, not 1 array. Accessing .[1] returns the first NDJSON line, not the array.
lessons.fix: Pre-wrap NDJSON: jq -s . file.ndjson > wrapped.json, then use jq --slurpfile dec wrapped.json and access $dec[0] as the array.

lessons.title: Even $TMPDIR can be cleared between Termux sessions
lessons.symptom: $TMPDIR/twgt-ei existed in one session but was gone on the next. Rebuild failed at first step with No such file or directory.
lessons.root_cause: Termux $TMPDIR (= $PREFIX/tmp) is not guaranteed to persist across sessions or pkg upgrade.
lessons.fix: For pipeline caches that must survive, use $PROJECT/.cache/<pipeline>/. Add .cache/ to .gitignore. Reserve $TMPDIR for genuinely ephemeral single-session scratch.

lessons.title: Network failures are not data-integrity failures
lessons.symptom: G06 failed on first strict run because 4 forks had PARENT_HEAD_UNREACHABLE from mobile network timeouts. On retry, 3 of those recovered but 3 different forks failed. A strict all-forks-ENRICHED gate would never pass reliably on Termux mobile.
lessons.root_cause: Termux on mobile networks has intermittent TLS/443 timeouts. Treating transient network errors as data-integrity failures makes the gate depend on network weather, not system state.
lessons.fix: Classify non-ENRICHED states as (a) structural failures (parent deleted, no common ancestor) → allowlist; (b) transient errors (network timeout, rate limit) → tolerate at commit and report count. Never conflate the two. Gate output must include both counts explicitly.
lessons.evidence: Run 1 non-ENRICHED: {5G-Proxy-Pro, hallmark, jsoncanvas, kepano-obsidian}. Run 2 non-ENRICHED: {5G-Proxy-Pro, sanitizers, Ventoid, open-design}. Only 5G-Proxy-Pro appears in both — the rest are network flake.

lessons.title: Registry snapshots are observations at time T, not assertions about now
lessons.symptom: M06 recorded unsloth as 6407 behind parent. Hours later, merge-upstream API reported not behind. Contradictory facts.
lessons.root_cause: The fork was synced between the two observations (either externally or via GitHub ruleset). M06 was correct at time T; the API is correct at T+N.
lessons.fix: When live API contradicts recorded registry data, re-run the observation to capture the new state. Commit the reconciliation. Never overwrite history silently.
lessons.evidence: M06 enriched.json: unsloth behind=6407. merge-upstream: not behind. Re-enrichment: behind=0, identical.

lessons.title: Anchor-based file insertion needs syntax verification
lessons.symptom: G06 inserted between G05 and array close, missing comma → SyntaxError: Unexpected token {
lessons.root_cause: Replacement text omitted the trailing comma that separates array elements.
lessons.fix: Run node --check after programmatic insertion; restore from git if syntax fails.
lessons.evidence: run.mjs line 96-97: closing brace followed immediately by G06 opening brace with no comma.

lessons.title: Sync success means state equals target, not state changed
lessons.symptom: M07 script warned 'Local HEAD did not change' after successful merge-upstream for caddy.
lessons.root_cause: Old code compared oldLocalSha to newLocalSha. If the fork was already synced between observations, both are equal and the script incorrectly warns.
lessons.fix: Compare newLocalSha to newParentSha. Record already_synced separately. G07 asserts success==true.
lessons.evidence: Caddy run: false warning despite merge-upstream success. Alacritty run: correct detection after propagation settled.

lessons.title: GitHub API propagation race — immediate re-observation may see stale state
lessons.symptom: After merge-upstream returned fast-forward for alacritty, immediate re-enrichment still reported fork as behind parent. remediation-latest.json recorded success:false. Re-running enrichment seconds later confirmed fork and parent HEADs identical.
lessons.root_cause: GitHub's merge-upstream returns before the fork's default-branch HEAD ref is fully propagated across GitHub's internal replicas. A read against /commits/ immediately after merge can return the pre-merge SHA.
lessons.fix: In p02-remediate.mjs: after merge-upstream, poll fork HEAD vs parent HEAD with exponential backoff (max 30s, 5 attempts) before re-enriching. If still divergent after 30s, write success:false and note the race. Do not silently accept stale observation.
lessons.evidence: Alacritty first attempt: 20c1e1b recorded success:false but re-enrichment showed identical. Root cause: propagation delay between merge-upstream response and /commits/ availability.

lessons.title: Heredoc node invocations must be chained with && or the shell continues after failure
lessons.symptom: M07.1 first patch attempt: node - <<'JS' exited with process.exit(1) because the string anchor 'const enriched = []' didn't exist (actual: 'const enriched = JSON.parse(...)'). The shell proceeded to the next node - <<'JS' which added G08 to run.mjs, and the subsequent git commit succeeded with 20 insertions — but the p02-remediate.mjs change was silently dropped.
lessons.root_cause: Sequential heredoc invocations in a shell block are separate commands. A non-zero exit from one does not stop the next unless the shell is running with set -e or the commands are chained with &&.
lessons.fix: Either: (a) prefix the whole session with set -e; (b) chain every node - <<'JS' with && node - <<'JS'; or (c) after any programmatic file patch, explicitly verify with grep that the change landed before proceeding.
lessons.evidence: Commit 45f65de: 1 file changed (run.mjs only), 20 insertions. But the intent was two files. The .mjs file was unchanged. Silent drop.

lessons.title: GitHub API propagation is per-endpoint, not global
lessons.symptom: PollUntil() succeeded at /commits/{branch} in 1621ms. Enrichment read stale fork state from /compare — fork appeared behind parent. 10+ minutes later, /compare still returned stale local_sha while /commits/{branch} returned correct SHA.
lessons.root_cause: GitHub caches fork /compare responses much longer than /commits/{branch} responses. This is not a short propagation window — it is a caching asymmetry between endpoints. /compare can serve stale fork refs for many minutes after /commits/{branch} has caught up.
lessons.fix: Enrichment must not trust /compare local_sha blindly. It should independently fetch /commits/{branch} for the fork and use that as the authoritative local_sha, only using /compare for ahead/behind counts. This is the M07.3 fix.
lessons.evidence: poll_ok: true. /commits/main returns b725ec00. /compare returns local=842c3098. Same fork, same branch, same moment — different answers.

lessons.title: Fetching fork HEAD directly via /commits bypasses /compare caching bug
lessons.symptom: After M07.2 discovered that /compare on forks serves stale local_sha for 10+ minutes, M07.3 implemented a fix: fetch fork HEAD via /commits/{branch}. Need to verify the fix works.
lessons.root_cause: GitHub's /compare endpoint caches fork commit refs aggressively. /commits/{branch} is cache-busted per request. Same fork, same moment, different answers.
lessons.fix: In p01-enrich-divergence.mjs: fetchForkHeadDirect(fullName, branch) calls /commits/{branch} and uses that as local_head_sha. /compare remains for ahead_by, behind_by, merge_base_sha — those are consistent within a single comparison.
lessons.evidence: docs fork: before fix, enrichment recorded local=842c3098 (stale from /compare). After full-file rewrite, local=b725ec00 (fresh, matches /commits/main). Full registry: 0 contradictory records after fix (was 78 — every up_to_date fork had local != parent). 78 consistent records match up_to_date count exactly. 12-min enrichment ran without error. G09 sampled 3 forks, all fresh.
lessons.additional_notes: Prior attempts: 45f65de (anchor not found), 3f9b4f2 (silently dropped), 56f586a (ReferenceError - declaration in if(!p.fork) block), plus 3 patch attempts this session (template-literal whitespace mismatches). Full-file rewrite succeeded where 8 patches failed. See L-PATCH-ANCHOR-FAIL.

lessons.title: Patch-by-string-anchor is fragile; full file rewrite is deterministic
lessons.symptom: Eight attempts to patch p01-enrich-divergence.mjs to add fetchForkHeadDirect and change two local_head_sha assignments. Every attempt failed: string anchors not found (whitespace mismatch), silent drop (heredoc exit did not halt shell), scope bug (declaration in wrong block), template-literal escaping (nested backticks in heredoc).
lessons.root_cause: src.includes(EXACT_STRING) requires the anchor to match byte-for-byte. Any prior edit shifts whitespace (tabs vs spaces, trailing spaces). Template literals with nested backticks need double-escaping that is fragile in heredocs. Any failure mode is invisible to grep -c which counts symbol presence, not scope or structure.
lessons.fix: For any file under 200 lines, use cat > file <<'EOF' to write the entire file. Verify with sed -n (visual inspection) and node --check (syntax). Use grep only to count total occurrences, not to verify scope or structure. Never patch anchors programmatically.
lessons.evidence: 8 patch attempts, 0 successes. 1 file rewrite, 1 success. 12-min enrichment completed with zero errors on first run after rewrite. Registry went from 78 contradictory records to 0.

lessons.title: A count is trustworthy only when produced by a structural parser
lessons.symptom: The session-close diagnostic script undercounted gates (9 instead of 10) because it used grep -oE 'id: "G[0-9]+"'. A human had to manually correct the count, recreating the very failure mode (L-PATCH-ANCHOR-FAIL) the session was trying to document.
lessons.root_cause: A single grep pattern is a hypothesis. It relies on formatting assumptions (e.g., id: "G10" vs id:'G10' vs { id: 'G10' }). Pattern matching cannot reliably parse structural data.
lessons.fix: Any reported count must be produced by a structural parser (e.g., importing the array in Node). If parsing is impossible, use two independently-written patterns and assert they agree. If a human touches the number, the artifact is not fail-closed. Generate close artifacts via script, never by hand.
lessons.evidence: Diagnostic script returned 9 gates. Manual inspection proved 10. G10 was invisible to the regex. See L-PATCH-ANCHOR-FAIL.

lessons.title: A claim of machine confirmation without the machine's output is a hypothesis
lessons.symptom: Session close artifacts and commit messages have repeatedly claimed tests passed or metrics were verified without the raw stdout/stderr being pasted in the same message. This creates authoritative-looking text that is not reproducible.
lessons.root_cause: Natural language is frictionless. Pasting raw terminal output is high-friction. When an AI assistant transcribes expected outputs, it creates a narrative that sounds like evidence but lacks cryptographic or structural proof.
lessons.fix: The One Command, One Paste rule: any claim of the form 'the machine confirmed X' must be accompanied by the verbatim raw output of the command that produced X, pasted in the same message, before any prose. If the output is not pasted, the claim is a hypothesis and must be labeled as such in commit messages.
lessons.evidence: Countless turns in this session where expected output was narrated as fact, culminating in a commit message asserting a negative test passed before the test was ever run.
